title: CTS Evangelism — Unit 2: The Nature of Evangelism (Bilingual)

blocks.en: 📖 Evangelism — Unit 2: The Nature of Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Evangelismo — Unidad 2: La Naturaleza del Evangelismo

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary · Dr. Wayne Cook, Author and Professor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Seminary Director
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala · Dr. Wayne Cook, Autor y Profesor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Director del Seminario

blocks.en: Orientation: Why Definitions Matter
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: Por Qué Importan las Definiciones

blocks.en: Having established the biblical foundation of evangelism in Unit 1, this unit turns to a question that often troubles sincere believers: What exactly is evangelism? Many Christians are active, passionate, and love the Lord, yet they struggle to share their faith because they have never been taught a clear definition. They may share a personal story or invite someone to church—both good things—but neither is the same as evangelism. Until the believer can name what evangelism is, he cannot do it well, nor can he know when he has finished.
blocks.es_reference: Habiendo establecido el fundamento bíblico del evangelismo en la Unidad 1, esta unidad aborda una pregunta que a menudo preocupa a los creyentes sinceros: ¿Qué es exactamente el evangelismo? Muchos cristianos son activos, apasionados y aman al Señor, pero luchan por compartir su fe porque nunca se les ha enseñado una definición clara. Pueden compartir una historia personal o invitar a alguien a la iglesia—ambas cosas buenas—pero ninguna es lo mismo que el evangelismo. Hasta que el creyente pueda nombrar qué es el evangelismo, no podrá hacerlo bien, ni sabrá cuándo ha terminado.

blocks.en: Real evangelism is something that is caught more than taught. It is a passion rather than a program. But a passion without a definition drifts; a program without a definition becomes activity for its own sake. This unit therefore lays down six word-pictures from the New Testament family of evangel, anchors evangelism in three classic definitions, and distinguishes it from manipulation, mere social action, and silent witness. When the foundation is biblical, the practice becomes both bold and humble.
blocks.es_reference: El verdadero evangelismo es algo que se capta más que se enseña. Es una pasión más que un programa. Pero una pasión sin definición se desvía; un programa sin definición se convierte en actividad por sí misma. Por lo tanto, esta unidad presenta seis imágenes verbales de la familia neotestamentaria del evangelio, ancla el evangelismo en tres definiciones clásicas, y lo distingue de la manipulación, la mera acción social y el testimonio silencioso. Cuando el fundamento es bíblico, la práctica se vuelve a la vez audaz y humilde.

blocks.en: I. The Family of "Evangel": Six Definitions
blocks.es_reference: I. La Familia del "Evangelio": Seis Definiciones

blocks.en: Behind the New Testament stands one Greek root—euangelion, "good news." From this single root six related terms grow, and a careful evangelist will hold each one distinct.
blocks.es_reference: Detrás del Nuevo Testamento se encuentra una raíz griega—euangelion, "buenas nuevas." De esta sola raíz crecen seis términos relacionados, y el evangelista cuidadoso mantendrá cada uno distinto.

blocks.en: Evangel. The evangel is the good news itself. It is not about death, hell, or sin in the first instance—those may be avenues to the good news, but the evangel proper is glad tidings: that Christ has died for sinners and risen again.
blocks.es_reference: Evangelio. El evangelio es la buena noticia misma. No trata principalmente de la muerte, el infierno o el pecado—esos pueden ser caminos hacia las buenas nuevas, pero el evangelio propio es buenas nuevas: que Cristo murió por los pecadores y resucitó.

blocks.en: "For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures" (1 Corinthians 15:3–4, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque primeramente os he enseñado lo que asimismo recibí: Que Cristo murió por nuestros pecados, conforme a las Escrituras; y que fue sepultado, y que resucitó al tercer día, conforme a las Escrituras." (1 Corintios 15:3–4, RVG)

blocks.en: Evangelism. Evangelism is the act of presenting the good news with the intent that people receive it. Evangelist. The evangelist is one who carries the good news. In one sense, every pastor is an evangelist, and the work may be done either publicly or personally. Evangelistic. Something is evangelistic when it is characterized by the urgent, active presentation of the good news. Evangelical. An evangelical is one who emphasizes the reception of the good news—one who endorses the work of evangelism. It is possible, the wise teacher observes, to be evangelical without being evangelistic. Evangelistic preaching. Faris Whitesell defined it: "Evangelistic preaching is preaching at its best. It is preaching adapted to the highest ends of the gospel—turning men from sin and darkness to salvation and light. Evangelistic preaching is preaching with a mission—an immediate and all-important mission—winning a verdict in favor of the Lord Jesus Christ."
blocks.es_reference: Evangelismo. El evangelismo es el acto de presentar las buenas nuevas con la intención de que la gente las reciba. Evangelista. El evangelista es quien lleva las buenas nuevas. En cierto sentido, todo pastor es un evangelista, y la obra puede hacerse pública o personalmente. Evangelístico. Algo es evangelístico cuando se caracteriza por la presentación urgente y activa de las buenas nuevas. Evangélico. Un evangélico es quien enfatiza la recepción de las buenas nuevas—quien apoya la obra del evangelismo. Es posible, observa el maestro sabio, ser evangélico sin ser evangelístico. Predicación evangelística. Faris Whitesell la definió: "La predicación evangelística es la predicación en su mejor expresión. Es la predicación adaptada a los fines más altos del evangelio—convertir a los hombres del pecado y las tinieblas a la salvación y la luz. La predicación evangelística es predicación con una misión—una misión inmediata y de suma importancia—ganar un veredicto a favor del Señor Jesucristo."

blocks.en: II. Three Classic Definitions
blocks.es_reference: II. Tres Definiciones Clásicas

blocks.en: Three definitions, set side by side, give the working frame for this course. The first comes from the Archbishop's Committee on Evangelism (1918):
blocks.es_reference: Tres definiciones, puestas lado a lado, dan el marco de trabajo para este curso. La primera viene del Comité del Arzobispo sobre Evangelismo (1918):

blocks.en: "To evangelize is so to present Jesus Christ in the power of the Holy Spirit that men shall come to put their trust in God through Him, to accept Him as their Savior, and to serve Him as their King in the fellowship of the Church."
blocks.es_reference: "Evangelizar es presentar a Jesucristo en el poder del Espíritu Santo de tal manera que los hombres lleguen a poner su confianza en Dios a través de Él, a aceptarle como su Salvador, y a servirle como su Rey en la comunión de la Iglesia."

blocks.en: Notice the careful balance: presenting Christ, in the Spirit's power, with the threefold goal of trust, acceptance, and service—within the church. The second comes from V. L. Stanfield: "Evangelistic preaching is the proclamation of the good news concerning the redemptive acts of God in Christ, by one who experientially knows Jesus Christ, in order to lead others to receive Jesus Christ as their Savior and their Lord." The third comes from D. T. Niles, and is the simplest of all: "Evangelism is one beggar telling another beggar where to get food." Niles' image is unforgettable. The evangelist is not a wealthy benefactor distributing favors; he is a hungry man who has found the bread, turning to another hungry man and pointing the way. This guards the witness from condescension and the gospel from being mistaken for moral superiority.
blocks.es_reference: Note usted el equilibrio cuidadoso: presentar a Cristo, en el poder del Espíritu, con el triple objetivo de confianza, aceptación y servicio—dentro de la iglesia. La segunda viene de V. L. Stanfield: "La predicación evangelística es la proclamación de las buenas nuevas concernientes a los actos redentores de Dios en Cristo, por alguien que conoce experimentalmente a Jesucristo, para llevar a otros a recibir a Jesucristo como su Salvador y su Señor." La tercera viene de D. T. Niles, y es la más simple de todas: "El evangelismo es un mendigo diciéndole a otro mendigo dónde conseguir comida." La imagen de Niles es inolvidable. El evangelista no es un benefactor rico distribuyendo favores; es un hombre hambriento que ha encontrado el pan, volviéndose a otro hombre hambriento y señalando el camino. Esto protege al testigo de la condescendencia y al evangelio de ser confundido con superioridad moral.

blocks.en: III. The Seven Propositions
blocks.es_reference: III. Las Siete Proposiciones

blocks.en: From years of pastoral ministry, seven propositions about evangelism deserve every student's reflection:
blocks.es_reference: De años de ministerio pastoral, siete proposiciones sobre el evangelismo merecen la reflexión de cada estudiante:

blocks.en: First, real evangelism is something that is caught more than taught. Second, real evangelism is a passion rather than a program. Third, as George Sweazy observed, a church always tends to drift away from evangelism, never toward it. Fourth, of every hundred conversions, only about fifteen take place at an event such as an evangelistic service or a crusade. Fifth, the average person hears the gospel about seven times before responding to Christ. Sixth, roughly eighty-five percent of converts have heard the gospel in a one-on-one setting. Seventh, a large portion of those who claim the name of Christ have become quietly ashamed of the gospel itself.
blocks.es_reference: Primera, el verdadero evangelismo es algo que se capta más que se enseña. Segunda, el verdadero evangelismo es una pasión más que un programa. Tercera, como observó George Sweazy, una iglesia siempre tiende a alejarse del evangelismo, nunca hacia él. Cuarta, de cada cien conversiones, solo unas quince tienen lugar en un evento como un servicio evangelístico o una cruzada. Quinta, la persona promedio oye el evangelio unas siete veces antes de responder a Cristo. Sexta, aproximadamente el ochenta y cinco por ciento de los convertidos han oído el evangelio en un encuentro personal, uno a uno. Séptima, una gran parte de los que claman el nombre de Cristo se han avergonzado silenciosamente del evangelio mismo.

blocks.en: These seven shape the rest of the course. They say to the student: do not despise the small conversation; do not measure the work by the crowd; do not be content with one telling; and do not lose the courage to name Christ where He has been forgotten.
blocks.es_reference: Estas siete dan forma al resto del curso. Le dicen al estudiante: no desprecie la conversación pequeña; no mida la obra por la multitud; no se contente con un solo decir; y no pierda el valor para nombrar a Cristo donde Él ha sido olvidado.

blocks.en: IV. Three New Testament Types
blocks.es_reference: IV. Tres Tipos del Nuevo Testamento

blocks.en: The New Testament shows at least three patterns of evangelism. The first is personal evangelism—the "go and tell" of the early house-to-house witness (Acts 5:42; 20:20). Done by both lay people and the pastor, it has been largely restored to the church only in the last few generations.
blocks.es_reference: El Nuevo Testamento muestra al menos tres patrones de evangelismo. El primero es el evangelismo personal—el "ir y decir" del temprano testimonio de casa en casa (Hechos 5:42; 20:20). Realizado tanto por laicos como por el pastor, ha sido restaurado a la iglesia en gran medida solo en las últimas generaciones.

blocks.en: The second is mass evangelism—the "come and see" of Pentecost and of the Whitefield-Wesley-Finney tradition. Whitefield was reported by contemporaries to have been heard clearly by crowds as large as thirty thousand; Wesley preached an estimated forty thousand sermons over his lifetime, learning his open-air method from Whitefield. The problem in the present age is not the method but the audience: fewer people today are willing to come.
blocks.es_reference: El segundo es el evangelismo masivo—el "venid y ved" de Pentecostés y de la tradición Whitefield-Wesley-Finney. Según reportes de sus contemporáneos, Whitefield podía ser oído claramente por multitudes de hasta treinta mil; Wesley predicó un estimado de cuarenta mil sermones en su vida, aprendiendo su método al aire libre de Whitefield. El problema en la época presente no es el método sino la audiencia: menos personas hoy están dispuestas a venir.

blocks.en: The third is lifestyle evangelism—the "go and live" approach Joseph Aldrich described. It is the rank-and-file Christian witnessing every day in natural relationships. A transformed life provokes the question, "How can I get what you have?"—and the believer answers with the gospel. None of the three replaces the others; the wise church practices all three.
blocks.es_reference: El tercero es el evangelismo como estilo de vida—el enfoque del "ir y vivir" que describió Joseph Aldrich. Es el cristiano común testificando todos los días en relaciones naturales. Una vida transformada provoca la pregunta: "¿Cómo puedo obtener lo que usted tiene?"—y el creyente responde con el evangelio. Ninguno de los tres reemplaza a los otros; la iglesia sabia practica los tres.

blocks.en: V. Evangelism Is Proclamation, Not Manipulation
blocks.es_reference: V. El Evangelismo Es Proclamación, no Manipulación

blocks.en: This distinction is critical. Some evangelistic methods press for a decision through emotional music, guilt, fear, or false promises of health and wealth. Such approaches are not evangelism; they are manipulation. Paul rejected these techniques:
blocks.es_reference: Esta distinción es crítica. Algunos métodos evangelísticos presionan por una decisión mediante música emotiva, culpa, miedo o falsas promesas de salud y riqueza. Tales enfoques no son evangelismo; son manipulación. Pablo rechazó estas técnicas:

blocks.en: "And my speech and my preaching were not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power." (1 Corinthians 2:4, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y ni mi palabra ni mi predicación fue con palabras persuasivas de humana sabiduría, sino con demostración del Espíritu y de poder." (1 Corintios 2:4, RVG)

blocks.en: He did not rely on clever methods but on the Spirit. The difference is trust: one trusts in technique, the other in God. A manipulative evangelist may produce a response, but the response is to pressure, not to Christ. A faithful evangelist presents truth clearly and allows the Spirit of God to do His work. When manipulation is used, the gospel itself is distorted—the good news becomes a sales pitch. Faithful witnesses therefore reject any method that pressures, deceives, or coerces.
blocks.es_reference: No confiaba en métodos ingeniosos sino en el Espíritu. La diferencia es la confianza: uno confía en la técnica, el otro en Dios. Un evangelista manipulador puede producir una respuesta, pero la respuesta es a la presión, no a Cristo. Un evangelista fiel presenta la verdad claramente y permite que el Espíritu de Dios haga su obra. Cuando se usa la manipulación, el evangelio mismo se distorsiona—las buenas nuevas se convierten en un discurso de ventas. Los testigos fieles, por lo tanto, rechazan cualquier método que presione, engañe o coaccione.

blocks.en: VI. Clarity Is Not Optional
blocks.es_reference: VI. La Claridad No Es Opcional

blocks.en: A vague message produces vague understanding. If a hearer does not understand who God is (holy, just, loving), what sin is (rebellion against a holy God), what Christ has done (died as a substitute and rose again), and what response is required (repentance and faith), then that hearer cannot be saved. Salvation is not a feeling; it is a response to truth understood. Therefore, when sharing the gospel, the believer should not assume prior knowledge. Christian jargon such as "born again" or "saved by grace" must be explained. Jesus Himself took time to explain the Scriptures to the Emmaus disciples (Luke 24:27). He did not rush. Neither should the modern evangelist. Clarity is an act of love and obedience.
blocks.es_reference: Un mensaje vago produce un entendimiento vago. Si un oyente no entiende quién es Dios (santo, justo, amoroso), qué es el pecado (rebelión contra un Dios santo), lo que Cristo ha hecho (murió como sustituto y resucitó), y qué respuesta se requiere (arrepentimiento y fe), entonces esa persona no puede ser salva. La salvación no es un sentimiento; es una respuesta a la verdad entendida. Por lo tanto, al compartir el evangelio, el creyente no debe asumir conocimiento previo. La jerga cristiana como "nacido de nuevo" o "salvo por gracia" debe ser explicada. Jesús mismo se tomó tiempo para explicar las Escrituras a los discípulos de Emaús (Lucas 24:27). No se apresuró. Tampoco debe hacerlo el evangelista moderno. La claridad es un acto de amor y obediencia.

blocks.en: VII. Faithfulness, Not Results
blocks.es_reference: VII. Fidelidad, No Resultados

blocks.en: One of the greatest misunderstandings in evangelism is that success is measured by visible results. Paul wrote:
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los mayores malentendidos en el evangelismo es que el éxito se mide por los resultados visibles. Pablo escribió:

blocks.en: "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase." (1 Corinthians 3:6, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Yo planté, Apolos regó; pero el crecimiento lo ha dado Dios." (1 Corintios 3:6, RVG)

blocks.en: Paul planted, Apollos watered—both were faithful. But the growth came from God. This is liberating. Many believers are paralyzed by the fear of failure: "What if I share and no one gets saved?" The seven propositions answer that fear. If the average person hears the gospel seven times before responding, the believer who shares once may be planting the seventh seed, the seed God will use—or he may be planting the first, which another will water and another harvest. None of the three has failed.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo plantó, Apolos regó—ambos fueron fieles. Pero el crecimiento vino de Dios. Esto es liberador. Muchos creyentes están paralizados por el miedo al fracaso: "¿Y si comparto y nadie se salva?" Las siete proposiciones responden ese miedo. Si la persona promedio oye el evangelio siete veces antes de responder, el creyente que comparte una vez puede estar plantando la séptima semilla, la semilla que Dios usará—o puede estar plantando la primera, que otro regará y otro cosechará. Ninguno de los tres ha fallado.

blocks.en: VIII. The Danger of Redefining Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: VIII. El Peligro de Redefinir el Evangelismo

blocks.en: In contemporary contexts, evangelism is often redefined to mean almost any good activity. Some say feeding the hungry is evangelism. Others say social justice is evangelism. Still others say a friendly presence is evangelism. These are good things, but they are not the gospel. Evangelism is the communication of the gospel. One can feed a thousand people and never mention why Christ died. One can fight for justice and never speak of the cross. One can be the kindest person in the neighborhood and never explain that "all have sinned" and that "Christ died for our sins." If the message is removed, evangelism itself is removed. Acts of mercy are vital, but they must be accompanied by the spoken truth. The greatest act of love is to tell a sinner how to be reconciled to God.
blocks.es_reference: En contextos contemporáneos, el evangelismo a menudo se redefine para significar casi cualquier actividad buena. Algunos dicen que alimentar al hambriento es evangelismo. Otros dicen que la justicia social es evangelismo. Otros dicen que una presencia amistosa es evangelismo. Estas son cosas buenas, pero no son el evangelio. El evangelismo es la comunicación del evangelio. Se puede alimentar a mil personas y nunca mencionar por qué Cristo murió. Se puede luchar por la justicia y nunca hablar de la cruz. Se puede ser la persona más amable del vecindario y nunca explicar que "todos han pecado" y que "Cristo murió por nuestros pecados." Si se elimina el mensaje, se elimina el evangelismo mismo. Las obras de misericordia son vitales, pero deben ir acompañadas de la verdad hablada. El mayor acto de amor es decirle a un pecador cómo ser reconciliado con Dios.

blocks.en: Conclusion: A Working Definition
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Una Definición de Trabajo

blocks.en: Bringing the threads together, this course adopts a working definition: Evangelism is the clear and faithful communication of the gospel, in the power of the Holy Spirit, with the intent that the hearer understand, believe, and follow Christ in the fellowship of the church. The definition unites Niles' simplicity, the Archbishop's Committee's balance, and Stanfield's precision. It rules out manipulation. It rules out silent presence as a sufficient substitute. It rules out redefinition as social action alone. And it places the work where Scripture places it: in the proclamation of one beggar to another, who together bow before the King.
blocks.es_reference: Uniendo los hilos, este curso adopta una definición de trabajo: El evangelismo es la comunicación clara y fiel del evangelio, en el poder del Espíritu Santo, con la intención de que el oyente entienda, crea y siga a Cristo en la comunión de la iglesia. La definición une la simplicidad de Niles, el equilibrio del Comité del Arzobispo y la precisión de Stanfield. Excluye la manipulación. Excluye la presencia silenciosa como sustituto suficiente. Excluye la redefinición como sola acción social. Y coloca la obra donde las Escrituras la colocan: en la proclamación de un mendigo a otro, que juntos se inclinan ante el Rey.

sa.prompt: Define the six terms in the evangel family (evangel, evangelism, evangelist, evangelistic, evangelical, evangelistic preaching) in your own words. Why does the unit insist that one can be evangelical without being evangelistic?
sa.model: The evangel family shares one root: the evangel is the good news itself; evangelism is the act of sharing it; an evangelist is the one who shares; evangelistic describes that activity; evangelical names sound gospel doctrine; and evangelistic preaching proclaims the good news for a verdict. One can be evangelical, holding right doctrine, without being evangelistic, actually sharing it — which is why the unit insists the two are not the same.

sa.prompt: State the Archbishop's Committee (1918) definition of evangelism in your own words. Identify the three elements of its goal (trust, accept, serve) and explain why the phrase 'in the fellowship of the Church' matters.
sa.model: The Archbishop's Committee defined evangelism as so presenting Christ that people come to put their trust in God through Him, to accept Him as Savior, and to serve Him as King in the fellowship of the Church. Its goal has three elements: trust, accept, and serve. The phrase 'in the fellowship of the Church' matters because conversion is not private; the new believer is brought into the community of God's people, not left alone.

sa.prompt: Explain D. T. Niles' definition: 'Evangelism is one beggar telling another beggar where to get food.' What does this image protect the evangelist from, and what does it protect the gospel from?
sa.model: Niles said evangelism is one beggar telling another beggar where to find food. The image protects the evangelist from pride, because a beggar has nothing of his own to boast in; he simply received bread by grace. And it protects the gospel from becoming a human achievement, because the food is a gift, freely given, that the beggar merely points others toward.

sa.prompt: List at least four of the seven propositions about evangelism from this unit, and explain why each shapes the work of the witness today.
sa.model: Among the seven propositions: evangelism is rooted in God's own initiative; it centers on the gospel of Christ, not on the messenger; it depends on the Holy Spirit and not human skill; it is the responsibility of every believer; and it must be governed by Scripture. Each shapes the witness today by keeping the work God-centered, gospel-centered, and Spirit-dependent rather than a human program.

sa.prompt: Distinguish the three New Testament types of evangelism (personal, mass, lifestyle). Why does the unit insist that none replaces the others?
sa.model: The New Testament shows three types: personal evangelism, one-on-one as Jesus did with the woman at the well; mass evangelism, public proclamation as at Pentecost; and lifestyle evangelism, the transformed life that provokes questions. None replaces the others because each reaches people the others cannot; together they form the full pattern of how the gospel spreads.

sa.prompt: Paul wrote that his preaching was 'not with persuasive words of human wisdom' (1 Corinthians 2:4, NKJV). Distinguish biblical persuasion from manipulation, and explain why manipulation distorts the gospel itself.
sa.model: Biblical persuasion appeals to the mind and conscience with truth, leaving the response free and trusting the Spirit to convict. Manipulation uses pressure, fear, or emotional trickery to force a decision. Manipulation distorts the gospel itself because the gospel is good news to be freely believed; coercing a response produces a false convert and misrepresents a God who invites rather than compels.

sa.prompt: The unit lists four elements that must be made clear in evangelism (who God is, what sin is, what Christ has done, what response is required). State all four and explain why a vague gospel produces a vague response.
sa.model: The four elements that must be made clear are who God is, what sin is, what Christ has done, and what response is required. A vague gospel produces a vague response because a hearer cannot trust what he does not understand; if God's holiness, his own sin, Christ's cross, and the call to repent and believe are blurred, any 'decision' rests on confusion rather than truth.

sa.prompt: If approximately 85% of conversions happen one-on-one and the average person hears the gospel about seven times before responding, what practical implications follow for the believer's daily witness?
sa.model: If most conversions happen one-on-one and people hear the gospel about seven times before responding, then the believer's daily, personal witness matters more than occasional events. It means being faithful in ordinary relationships, expecting to be one of several voices over time rather than the single decisive one, and not growing discouraged when a first conversation bears no visible fruit.

sa.prompt: The unit warns against three common redefinitions of evangelism (feeding the hungry, social justice, friendly presence) as substitutes for the gospel itself. Why are these good things dangerous when allowed to replace evangelism?
sa.model: Feeding the hungry, pursuing social justice, and being a friendly presence are good things, but they are dangerous when allowed to replace evangelism because they can quiet the conscience into thinking the gospel has been shared when no one has heard the message of Christ. Good deeds may open a door, but they cannot save; only the proclaimed gospel does. When the good replaces the essential, people are served in body but lost in soul.

sa.prompt: State the unit's working definition of evangelism and explain how it unites Niles' simplicity, the Archbishop's Committee's balance, and Stanfield's precision while ruling out manipulation and redefinition.
sa.model: The unit's working definition is that evangelism is sharing the good news of Christ so that people come to trust, accept, and serve Him within the fellowship of the Church. It unites Niles' simplicity (one beggar telling another), the Archbishop's Committee's balance (trust, accept, serve in the Church), and Stanfield's precision (a clear gospel content), while ruling out manipulation, which forces response, and redefinition, which substitutes good deeds for the message.
